open_points.subject: start_and_recover_kernel / installed-instance collision check
open_points.text: `capability:bindings.check_installed_instances`: no credential header has, case-insensitively, the name of a required header of its instance (A09 rule 1).
open_points.question: How does `bindings.check_installed_instances` obtain the complete set of configured services (and their credential header names) to check, given State 3 lists only `selected_instance_name`, `resolve_service_credential`, and `manifest_source` on `module:installation`?
options: `installation` exposes an iteration/list capability over configured services
`bindings` infers services by scanning manifest records
`bindings` checks only services referenced elsewhere at startup
open_points.default_guess: Add/assume an `installation` capability that enumerates configured services and their credential-header names.

open_points.subject: run_read_only_flow / request building for file inputs
open_points.text: `capability:service_invoker.prepare_request` judges the instance, resolves the credential ... and places the inputs, JSON values as `capability:canonical_values.canonical_bytes`
open_points.question: For a `read` operation using `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH` with `file` inputs (allowed by A09 rule 2), which module reads file bytes (including spooled files) and passes them into request construction in this flow?
options: `effects` reads file bytes via `store.read_value_bytes` before `prepare_request` (as stated in `flow:run_effect_with_approval`)
open_points.default_guess: Reuse the `run_effect_with_approval` pattern: `effects` reads file bytes via `store.read_value_bytes` and passes them to `service_invoker`.

open_points.subject: author_and_admit_function / add_trial_case partial-write failure
open_points.text: Value bytes and file fixtures go to the content-addressed area through `capability:store.put_value_bytes` ... and the TrialCase in one `capability:store.record_change`.
open_points.question: If one or more `put_value_bytes` calls succeed but the subsequent `record_change` fails, are those newly written bytes kept as unreferenced content or rolled back/cleaned up?
options: Keep unreferenced bytes (immutable content area, no cleanup)
Attempt compensating cleanup of just-written bytes
Treat as impossible by requiring single transactional primitive across bytes+record
open_points.default_guess: Keep unreferenced bytes, consistent with the stated behavior for refused capture-copy bytes.
